title: A 20-Inch Shark Took Bites Out of Nuclear Submarines

scenes.text: A shark the size of your forearm bit nuclear submarines.
The cookiecutter shark. Twenty inches. It rises from the deep at night.
It latches on with suction lips, spins, and twists out a perfectly round plug of flesh.
Whales, dolphins, tuna, even great whites. All carry the round scars.
In the 1970s it bit the rubber sonar domes of US Navy submarines. The subs went blind.
Its belly glows green, except one dark collar shaped like a small fish. Bait.

description:
The cookiecutter shark grows to only about 50 centimetres but takes neat, round plugs of flesh out of whales, dolphins, tuna, seals and great white sharks.
In the 1970s, reports say, the sharks bit into the rubber-covered sonar domes of US Navy submarines, leaking the sound-transmitting oil and forcing repairs, until the Navy fitted fiberglass covers. The shark's glowing belly hides it from below, while a dark collar may act as a lure.
Which sea creature would you least want to meet at night? Comment below.
first_comment: Its lower teeth are the biggest of any shark relative to body size, and it sheds the whole row at once and swallows it to recycle the calcium. Which shark fact surprised you most?
